anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink or beacon call. In this case the value is constructed inside the flush drain timer callback, after the queue is drained and materialized, so the enqueue-stage digest helpers are not the anchor.

primary_anchor.source_export: private helper reached through exported u(config)
primary_anchor.why: Constructs the target batch_token inside the flush drain timer callback by folding the context flag score, tuple score and runtime ticket into the reducer variant selection, then combining the reducer result with the batch payload frame and the 16-char base36 token encoder into the bk_ batch token that is placed into the analytics.flush object and the /api/collect/batch beacon body. The enqueue-stage digest, the envelope composer and the beacon transport are all downstream or off-chain.
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only: the canonical anchor answer is captured_span plus answer_function as declared in the captured bundle slice. source_function is a private maintainer mapping into src/.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle (hash/offset/complete function body). Agents only see captures, so the standard answer identifier is primary_anchor.answer_function, not source_function.

A returned function name is scored against answer_function in the captured corpus. source_function is a private maintainer label and is not something an agent can know unless the bundle still exposes that exact identifier.
Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from the enqueue digest helper, the drain scheduler, the runtime config materializer and the beacon/console sink to qualify for full credit.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_default_agent_corpus; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing span

do_not_promote: The final console sink and beacon call site emit an already constructed batch_token value.
The exported factory only wraps the private batch payload anchor and should not outrank the anchor itself.
The enqueue-stage entry digest is a nested helper on the material path but constructs the per-entry digest, not the target batch token; it sits one 0.7 tier below the anchor.
The prefetch beacon token generator is fired at enqueue time and is off the target chain.
The shadow flush emitter writes a bk_-styled fake frame and is off the target chain.
Non-target analytics-style console objects carry beacon_ref/queue_ref values that never equal the target batch token.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Returned span maps uniquely to primary_anchor.captured_span; answer_function matches the buildBatchPayloadToken declaration in that captured bundle slice.
Returned span maps to a target-specific helper below the anchor, such as encodeBatchToken, batchTokenFrame, batchPayloadFrame, runReducer or the enqueue-stage computeEntryDigest.
Returned span maps to a generic utility directly used by the token construction path, or the base36 folder and envelope serializer reused across chains.
Returned span maps to a path-critical dispatcher/materializer (drain scheduler, timer callback host, config materializer, middleware, sink wrapper) or the exported factory.
Returned span maps to a path-generic helper (tuple unpack, control reader, context snapshot, outbox drain).
Returned span maps to an off-chain decoy (shadow emitter, prefetch token, decoy launcher) or nothing on the behavior chain.
